records.name: Turks and Caicos Islands
records.summary:
Turks and Caicos decriminalised same-sex activity in 2001 through the UK-imposed Caribbean reform, and its constitution now bans discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation. The live frontier has been recognition rather than criminal law: the Court of Appeal ordered a residence permit for the same-sex spouse lawfully married abroad, holding that 'spouse' in the immigration ordinance must include same-sex spouses and declaring violations of the equality, non-discrimination and private-and-family-life guarantees — while declining to touch the constitution's male-female marriage definition, which it treated as controlling.

The administering state's passport guidance maintains a standing profile of the territory's rules on marriage, civil partnerships, adoption and gender recognition. Socially, a resident's account described 'virtually nothing' documented about gay life — in a territory where around two-thirds of inhabitants are themselves not native-born — so visitor experience runs on privacy and the resort economy rather than any visible scene.

sources.summary: GlobalGayz resident account ('Eddi', May 2009): documents how invisible gay life is — 'virtually nothing on the Internet about gay life in TCI'; notes ~2/3 of residents are not originally from the islands and full-citizen Belongers are a demographic minority versus foreigners, so there is no visible scene and privacy is the norm; useful as the on-the-ground social-climate read for a visitor.

UK HM Passport Office knowledge-base profile (Crown copyright 2025): official operational guidance covering nationality, legitimacy, adoption, gender recognition, civil partnerships and marriage, and documents for the territory — states adoption is legal and that 'transgender citizens are recognised in the Turks and Caicos Islands', i.e. the administering state's passport office handles gender-recognised documents for this jurisdiction.

TC Weekly News: Court of Appeal landmark ruling ordered the Director of Immigration to issue a residence permit to Timothy Haymon as the same-sex spouse of Richard Sankar — refusal on sexual-orientation grounds contravened constitutional guarantees; 'spouse' in the Immigration Ordinance read to include a same-sex spouse lawfully married in another jurisdiction, with equality/non-discrimination/private-life guarantees invoked (marriage definition left untouched). Directly relevant: same-sex partners of visitors/residents get residence recognition.

Klshepedia overview (published Apr 2026): same-sex sexual activity legal in the Turks and Caicos Islands since 2001 and discrimination on sexual-orientation grounds is constitutionally banned — the two anchor legal facts for a visitor assessing exposure.

records.name: Falkland Islands
records.summary:
South Atlantic island settlement with its own assembly: same-sex activity legal since 1989, equal age of consent since 2005, and full equality in April 2017 when the assembly approved same-sex marriage and civil partnerships 7-1, on a public consultation showing 90 per cent support for marriage and 94 per cent for partnerships — the registrar confirmed the law the following June, adoption followed the same year, the constitution bans sexual-orientation discrimination, and the first Pride was held in the capital that April. An official of the community described it as 'open, tolerant and respectful'; note that the much more remote dependencies administered from the same capital did not follow on marriage.

The earlier profile's inherited arithmetic and its borrowed UK custody stories have been deleted: on the surviving evidence the legal picture here is stronger, not weaker, than the administering state's, and there is no source indicating the GB single-sex-services code extends to the territory.

sources.summary: PinkNews (12 Apr 2017): the Legislative Assembly passed same-sex marriage (7-1) plus civil partnerships open to same-sex AND opposite-sex couples, after a public consultation showing 90% support for same-sex marriage and 94% for civil partnerships in the ~3,000-resident territory — the operative equality reform.

Rob Salerno blog (22 Jun 2017): direct confirmation from the Falklands registrar general that the March-passed same-sex marriage and civil partnership bill is law (royal-assent confusion resolved by her reply); same registrar confirms same-sex marriage is NOT legal in the South Georgia and South South Sandwich Islands dependency.

Mirror summary of the Wikipedia LGBTQ rights page (wiki-derived): legal since 1989, equal age of consent since 2005; same-sex marriage and civil partnerships since 29 April 2017; stepchild and joint adoption since 2017; constitutional ban on sexual-orientation discrimination; UK responsible for defence; attitudes largely positive (90% consultation support).
